sermon.title: Saved From Our Enemies
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches the fifth promise, that believers will be saved from their enemies (Luke 1:70–75). He covers positional versus conditional righteousness, the story of Terah and Abraham stopping halfway and the call to go on, God’s promise to bless all families, turning people from sin, and Esther and David.

chunks.section_question: What does he mean that God is who the Bible says he is? (Philippians 4:13, Romans 8:37)

If that is true and you really believe that, then God is who the Bible says he is, not who you say he is. God is who the Bible says he is, can I get an amen? I don’t need motivational speaking every Sunday, I need Jesus and I need the living word every Sunday. See, I am who God says I am, and the Bible says we are more than conquerors, and more than a conqueror comes through the battle without even a wound. Hallelujah. I can be and do what God says I can be and do, and that ends it.

chunks.section_question: What is the fifth promise, and who are the enemies? (Luke 1:70–75)
chunks.short_answer: He says “fifth promise: we will be saved from our enemies,” and that the enemies “are the children of the wicked one… people who oppose and hate the Bible, they hate Jesus.” He says the victory comes “now, in this life, and all the days of my life,” and “I don’t need to get raptured out to get out of this mess.” He distinguishes these enemies from Satan and sin, covered in earlier promises.
chunks.text:
Now, you ready for this message? Hallelujah. I don’t like it when people come to church to socialize and go through the motions. Church is not a place to socialize and go through the motions, it’s a place to release the rivers of God, where people can get healing on their inner man, physical healing, grow in God. The church is a place where Jesus is to be exalted, Jesus is to move, Jesus is to do things. Can I hear an amen? So, fifth promise: we will be saved from our enemies. Luke 1, verse 70-75: God spoke to his prophets which have been since the world began.

So Adam and Eve, Adam was a prophet, Eve was a prophetess, since the world began God’s been speaking through his prophets. Are you there? And he doesn’t lie, and what these prophets said is God’s word, that ends it. So what did he say since the world began? God said that we should be saved from our enemies and from the hand of all that hate us. Now, we’re living in a generation in America where we got a lot of enemies and a lot of people that hate the real church, the real Christian, and God said we would be saved from all our enemies. The prophet said that God would perform the mercy promised here. Here’s the promise, okay: “to our fathers and remember his holy covenant.”

So God promised he would save us from all our enemies and all that hate us, he promised he would remember his holy covenant, the oath which he swore to our father Abraham. Verse 74: “that he would grant unto us that we, being delivered out of the hand of our enemies, might serve him without fear.” Now, we know Satan is our enemy, but we dealt with that in the first promise. We know that sin is our enemy, we dealt with that in the second promise. So who are these enemies here? These enemies here are the children of the wicked one, as it says in the parable in Matthew, the enemy that sowed them is the Devil, the tares, the children of the wicked one.

They are people who oppose and hate the Bible, they hate Jesus, and they hate anybody and oppose anybody that wants to follow them. So these enemies he’s talking about is the children of the wicked one, that we can serve him without fear in holiness and righteousness before him all the days of our life. So when is this victory over our enemy supposed to happen? In this life, not in the rapture. I don’t need to get raptured out to get out of this mess and all that. I have a God that promised me that I would have victory over my enemies and over those that hate me now, in this life, and all the days of my life, not just a little season in my life but all the days of my life. I have victory over my enemies and those that hate me. Are you there?

chunks.section_question: What does he say about positional and conditional righteousness? (Luke 1:75)
chunks.short_answer: He says most Christians in America “are only righteous positionally by the blood,” and “God wants it to be a condition, not just a position.” He says “the position is important while you’re growing,” but “the condition is the goal,” and that without it “they live weak Christian lives.”
chunks.text:
And God can’t lie, and he is who he said he was, and we can be who he said we could be, all right. A lot of Christians have embraced this, and a lot of them haven’t. And let me give you a little word of wisdom: most Christians in America, because of ministers, are only righteous positionally by the blood. You see, he says “holiness and righteousness all the days of my life.”

They never get to where that righteousness and holiness is a condition in their life, and God wants it to be a condition, not just a position, and so they live loosely and they live weak Christian lives, because, “Well, I’m saved by the blood, I’m, you know, hallelujah, everything’s by the blood,” I don’t embrace anything, I don’t change my speech, I don’t change my attitude, I’m just saved by the blood. I submit to you this morning, victory over your enemy is getting righteousness conditionally, you possess it in your life, and he said you could do that, and what God says is true. Amen. The position is important while you’re growing, that you don’t get cast down and excommunicate yourself, but the condition is the goal. That’s what’s going to help you in life, that’s what’s going to help your family, that’s what’s going to help your community, that’s what’s going to help the church and your nation, is you getting to a condition of righteousness.

chunks.section_question: What does he say about the city and tower of Babel? (Genesis 11:1–9)
chunks.short_answer: He says “no one ever talks about the city, they always talk about the tower,” and that “because they’re one, nothing is impossible for them.” He says God scattered the people, “that’s where your races came from,” and he challenges evolution “from logic.” His claims about the origin of peoples and about science are his own and are not verified here.
chunks.text:
Okay, they migrated down here and decided to build a tower. And this is what they said: “Let us build a city.” No one ever talks about the city, they always talk about the tower. But they said, “Let us build a city, then let us build a tower that reaches to the heavenlies,” a platform. And then they said, “Let us build us a name.” Oh, their name was supposed to be above all names, not God. And then they said, “We want to do this so we’re not scattered throughout the earth.” And what did God want from the day Adam and Eve were born? Scattered. Yeah, multiply, replenish, fill the earth. They didn’t want to scatter, they wanted to stay united.

chunks.section_question: What does he say the church’s goal is, according to Acts 3? (Acts 3:25–26)
chunks.short_answer: He says Christ came “to turn people from their sin, not to keep them in their sin as a position,” and “if the church is not turning people from sin, we’re not doing our job.” He applies this to homosexuality, saying “Jesus will deliver you from that sin,” and adds claims about hell and disease that are his own. chunks.section_question: What does “possess the gate of his enemies” mean, and what do Esther and David show? (Genesis 22:17, Esther 9:1, Psalm 18:17)
chunks.short_answer: He says “the gate is where the leaders held their courts,” so God’s promise means taking it “to them.” He cites Esther and Mordecai and says “we got to be like Esther,” and David’s deliverance in Psalm 18:17. He says “just because we’re a small church doesn’t mean we can’t have a message to America,” and to say “God, here I am, use me.”
chunks.text:
The gate is where the judgment took place, the gate is where the leaders held their courts and all that was at the gate, all right, “and you will possess the gate of your enemy.” You’re not out 50 miles from the city, you’re there at the gate, you’re taking it to them. Now, I want to show you that it happened. There’s many places where this happened, I just want to show you real quick in Esther chapter 9, verse 1: the enemies of the Jews hoped to have power over the Jews, but it turned to the contrary, that the Jews had rule over them that hated them. See, did God fulfill his word? Yeah. And this woman minister was the key, Esther, she was a key to this. Mordecai, her uncle, was also a key. The Jews smote all their enemies and did what they would unto those that hated them. You see, God not only promised it but he also fulfilled the promise, and will he fulfill the promise to us?

Yes, but we’ve got to know the goal, we’ve got to get involved, we got to be like Esther, we got to get involved. Esther had to come out of her uncle’s house and go into the king’s palace, she had to do some things that she didn’t want to do. Mordecai was taken captive and drug, forced into the land of Babylon, a great man, a holy man, a righteous man, and raised Esther to be right, he had to do some things he didn’t want to do so that God’s plan could be executed. And if we get so stuck in just being an American, you know, that has two cars and a garage and everything going for us, we’ve got to come out of that box and say, “God, here I am, use me.” Could that be an amen?

See, then the Jews backed up Esther and Mordecai, a man and woman team. Psalm 18:17: “He delivered me.” This is David talking. David was chased by Saul, he was chased by the Philistines, he was chased by the people of Israel, they all wanted to kill him and they wanted to destroy him, and in Psalm 18 David said God delivered me “from my strong enemy and from them which hated me, for they were too strong for me.” How many, you know, right now in America the humanist and the homosexual activists and the atheists and all that seem to have the upper hand. You see, can we turn that around? Yeah, if we understand God’s promise. We don’t have to sit idly by. I don’t care, you know, Bible says there’s nothing for God to say by many or by few. Just because we’re a small church doesn’t mean we can’t have a message to America.

chunks.section_question: How does he say the promise is carried out? (Luke 1:71, 2 Thessalonians 2)
chunks.short_answer: He says “we can start with our neighbors, we can start with our family,” and that the key is worship: “they should see us all worshiping Jesus.” He says the Bible tells us “to lift our hands, lift our voices, sing unto God.” He ends: “let’s don’t stop halfway in the journey… let God make us a spiritual temple and build his kingdom in us.”
chunks.text:
Is that an amen? Or to our community. We don’t have to wait for America, we can start with our neighbors, we can start with our family. We can tell a man, “You are who God said you are, and you can be who God said you can be.” We can start turning this tide around. Now, going back to Luke 1:71: “We shall be saved from our enemies and all that hate us, we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear, in holiness and righteousness before him all the days of our life.” So how we going to do this thing? Okay, we got to accept the fact that God is who he said he was, he’ll do what he said he would do, we are who God said we are, and we can do and be what God said we could do and be.

So the key here is how we got to serve him, worship him. See, when people come into this church they should see us all worshiping Jesus. I told you over and over and over, you knew who a Muslim is by how they worship, you know who a Hindu is and a Buddha is by how they worship. You see, you know who a person is on his own throne and set himself up as God, as it says in Thessalonians. We think that’s one individual, the son of perdition, but it’s you playing God over your life.

You make your rules, and so when you are not following Bible methods of worship and prayer and all this, the people come in and they say, “You as is a different God.” Are you there? Young people, you getting this? You want people to touch God, do what God says to do, they will be directed right to him, not to you. The Bible says that we are to lift our hands, lift our voices, sing unto God, we’re to shout unto God, we’re to stand in the house of the Lord and worship him. We are, you know, to play our musical instrument. Music is a big part in this thing God is doing, and his music is important, not the secular music or not our special popular music, but his music is very important. He chose music and singing. Hallelujah.

And when people come in and they see us united worshiping God, seeking our God, they will be blessed and they will be touched and they can be healed in their inner man. Let’s all read this together: “God cannot lie. The Bible is his word. God is who the Bible says he is. He’ll do what the Bible says he will do. We are who the Bible says we are. We can do and be what the Bible says we can do and be.” Can I hear an amen? faqs.question: Does he say God will do what the Bible says he will do?
faqs.answer: Yes. He says “God is who he says he is, and God will do what he said he would do,” and that he said he would bring us into the divine nature.

faqs.question: What does he mean by “more than a conqueror”?
faqs.answer: He says “more than a conqueror comes through the battle without even a wound.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Yet in all these things we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us.

faqs.question: What does he say church is not for?
faqs.answer: He says “I don’t like it when people come to church to socialize and go through the motions,” and calls church “a place to release the rivers of God.”

faqs.question: Who does he say the “enemies” in Luke 1 are?
faqs.answer: He says “these enemies here are the children of the wicked one,” people who “oppose and hate the Bible.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: To grant us that we, Being delivered from the hand of our enemies, Might serve Him without fear,

faqs.question: When does he say victory over enemies happens?
faqs.answer: He says it is “now, in this life,” and “all the days of my life,” not only at the rapture.

faqs.question: What does he mean by positional righteousness?
faqs.answer: He says it means being “righteous positionally by the blood,” and that God wants righteousness to be “a condition, not just a position.”

faqs.question: Does he say the church should be involved in government?
faqs.answer: He says “after Jesus and sin, government is the most talked about subject in the Bible,” and asks, “how are we going to rule over our enemies if we’re not in places of authority?” This is his view.

faqs.question: Does he say Jesus’s death only covers sin?
faqs.answer: No. He calls that idea “something wrong with that mentality,” saying the best Jesus can do is give “the promises that he promised you.”

faqs.question: Does he say problems mean a lack of faith?
faqs.answer: No. He says “going through problems isn’t a sign you’re lacking faith and you’re not a good Christian.”

faqs.question: Why does he say God scattered the people at Babel?
faqs.answer: He says “because they’re one, nothing is impossible for them,” so God came down, “confounded the language,” and scattered them across the earth.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then they said to one another, “Come, let us make bricks and bake them thoroughly.” They had brick for stone, and they had asphalt for mortar. And they said, “Come, let us build ourselves a city, and a tower whose top is in the heavens; let us make a name for ourselves, lest we be scattered abroad over the face of the whole earth.” But the LORD came down to see the city and the tower which the sons of men had built. And the LORD said, “Indeed the people are one and they all have one language, and this is what they begin to do; now nothing that they propose to do will be withheld from them. Come, let Us go down and there confuse their language, that they may not understand one another’s speech.” So the LORD scattered them abroad from there over the face of all the earth, and they ceased building the city. Therefore its name is called Babel, because there the LORD confused the language of all the earth; and from there the LORD scattered them abroad over the face of all the earth.

faqs.question: Why does it matter that Terah stopped in Haran?
faqs.answer: He says “Terah gets the family and takes them up to Haran, and then he stops there, and the whole family stops because Daddy stopped,” and “you got to rise above your family.”

faqs.question: Why does he say God told Abraham to leave his father’s house?
faqs.answer: He says “father was worshiping other gods,” and God told Abraham “you got to complete the journey, you got to reach the goal.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now the LORD had said to Abram: “Get out of your country, From your family And from your father’s house, To a land that I will show you.

faqs.question: What does he say it means to be a blessing?
faqs.answer: He says “you’re going to do good to other people, you’re going to cause them to want the God that you serve.”

faqs.question: Does he say a small church can make a difference?
faqs.answer: He says “just because we’re a small church doesn’t mean we can’t have a message to America,” and “we don’t have to wait for America.”
